requirements.text: move the case to someone within the group who currently has the lightest workload or had lightest workload in past
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 4 AND assigned_to = 33 AND assignment_group = 7 AND status = 'awaiting_acceptance' AND request_status = 'requested'
assumptions: HRC0000714 is hr_case_id 4, in work_in_progress, assigned to user 6 (Stephanie Todd) and group 7 (Network Infrastructure); user 6 belongs to group 2 only, so the current assignee is outside the case's group
group 7 has two members, user 29 (Anne Medina) and user 33 (Zachary Mcintosh); neither has an open case or open task, so current workload ties at zero
past workload breaks the tie: user 29 has one closed case and two closed tasks, user 33 none, so the case goes to user 33
the case stays in its group: the request moves it to someone within the group, so assignment_group remains 7
status awaiting_acceptance and request_status requested: the policy requires both when a case is assigned to a user, and work_in_progress to awaiting_acceptance is an allowed transition
user 33 is already a member of group 7, so the policy's add-to-group step does not apply

disagreement: assignment_group: one pass tests 7, the other leaves it untested; chose 7, the tighter predicate, because the request keeps the case within its group and group 7 is the case's group on the seed

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 61 AND hr_case_id = 4 AND email = 'zachary.mcintosh3@servicenow.com' AND type = 'update'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest notification_id in the seed is 60); the task creates exactly one notification
him is the new assignee, user 33, whose email is zachary.mcintosh3@servicenow.com
type update kept from the benchmark check; the request does not name a type, and 'update him' matches it

notes:
disagreement: value: the case's assignment_group: one pass tests 7, the other leaves it untested; kept 7, the tighter predicate, because the request moves the case to someone within its group and the case is in group 7 on the seed.
The acting user is Karen Watkins (user 39, admin), who may reassign cases.
The case row carries org_id 4 while group 7 and its members carry org_id 1; the request and the benchmark both treat group 7 as the case's team, so the file does too.
The notification's status is not fixed by the request or the policy and is not tested.
